script: This Renaissance boy band is hiding a massive secret. This is Caravaggio’s 'The Musicians', painted in 1597. On the surface, it’s just four young guys getting ready for a music rehearsal. But look closer. It’s basically a 16th-century photoshoot, and Caravaggio is playing some major mind games here. First off, see the boy in the background, second from the right, looking straight at us? That’s actually a self-portrait of Caravaggio himself! He's photobombing his own painting. Next, check out the kid on the left with the wings and the grapes. That's Cupid. But he's not looking very angelic, is he? He's totally ignoring the music to sneak a snack. Now look at the boy in the front with his back to us. Caravaggio's mastery of light—that classic dramatic chiaroscuro—makes his bare back practically glow, pulling you right into the middle of the huddle. And see that unused violin sitting right at the bottom? It’s an open invitation. It’s like Caravaggio is asking: 'Well, are you going to pick it up and play with us, or just stand there?' What do you think, would you join this band?
